issue: Tip overgeneralizes: '-μαι verbs form the future in -ηθώ' is false as a rule — έρχομαι → θα έρθω (taught 14 cards later at el-0575), κάθομαι → θα κάτσω, μοιράζομαι → θα μοιραστώ. A learner applying it produces *ερχηθώ. Only the κοιμάμαι/φοβάμαι/θυμάμαι class takes -ηθώ. Sentence itself is perfect.

fix.english: Tonight I'll go to sleep early.
fix.grammar: κοιμάμαι-type verbs make the future in -ηθώ: θα κοιμηθώ (tha kimithó = I'll sleep).

issue: Gloss fidelity: 'will make pita' — English readers parse 'pita' as flatbread, but Greek πίτα here is the savory filo pie (τυρόπιτα/χορτόπιτα family) a grandmother bakes. The gloss should say 'pie', with a tip fencing off the false friend.

fix.target: Η γιαγιά θα φτιάξει πίτα για όλους.
fix.english: Grandma will make a pie for everyone.
fix.grammar: πίτα (píta) = a savory filo pie — τυρόπιτα, σπανακόπιτα — not flatbread.

issue: Tip romanization breaks the deck's phonemic scheme: 'kataláveis' transliterates the spelling ει instead of the sound /i/ (cf. 'tha dis', 'kimithó', 'isitíria' elsewhere). Should be katalávis. Sentence and aspect are fine.

fix.target: Το μωρό θα μεγαλώσει πριν το καταλάβεις.
fix.english: The baby will grow up before you know it.
fix.grammar: πριν + future-type form: πριν το καταλάβεις (prin to katalávis = before you know it).

issue: Food-vocabulary precision: the dish is τα γεμιστά, grammatically plural on every taverna menu; singular 'το γεμιστό' is not how anyone asks about it, and the gloss 'the stuffed vegetable' is equally unidiomatic English.

fix.grammar: τα γεμιστά (ta ʝemistá) — rice-stuffed tomatoes and peppers; the dish name is always plural.

issue: 'Το ψάρι έχει τιμή με το κιλό' is a clunky calque of 'is priced by the kilo'; a waiter or local says το ψάρι πάει με το κιλό (or χρεώνεται με το κιλό). The excellent cultural tip is kept.

fix.target: Το ψάρι πάει με το κιλό.
fix.english: The fish is priced by the kilo.
fix.grammar: fresh fish at tavernas goes με το κιλό (me to kiló = by the kilo) — ask the price before you order.

issue: Gloss mismatch: Greek says κάτω από το τραπέζι (under the table) but the English says 'under the table leg' — and the leg is the point: the wobbly-taverna-table paper wedge goes κάτω από το πόδι του τραπεζιού. As written, target and gloss describe different acts.

fix.target: Βάζουμε ένα χαρτί κάτω από το πόδι του τραπεζιού.
fix.english: We put a piece of paper under the table leg.
fix.grammar: το πόδι του τραπεζιού (to pódi tu trapeziú = the table leg) — the classic fix for a wobbly taverna table.
